A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same JE/AIS/RDS research work. Their main text, equations, algorithms, figures, and complete appendices support reliable comparison, including matching retained material across renumbering and relocation.

before.justification: V1 reports theoretical results and proofs, including an analytical Gaussian-mixture example, but no original experimental or simulation outcomes.

after.justification: V2 reports original normalizing-constant estimates and sampling results for two multimodal distributions in Table 1, Figures 2–3, and Appendix I.

M1.justification: V2 makes a localized but consequential correction to the RDS estimator: Algorithm 2's final work update changes +(T−δ)d to −(T−δ)d, consistently with Theorem 5. This changes the returned estimate. The AIS procedure and four RDS score-estimation approaches otherwise remain; those approaches already appeared in v1 Appendix E.5.

E1.justification: V2 introduces actual evaluations on a modified Müller Brown distribution and an unequal-weight, four-component Gaussian mixture, both in two dimensions. V1 contains no empirical coverage; its Gaussian-mixture counterexample is theoretical.

E2.justification: Table 1 introduces measured comparisons of TI and AIS against RDMC, RSDMC, ZODMC, and SNDMC on both targets. These methods were discussed in v1, but none participated in a reported empirical comparison there.

E3.justification: Appendix I introduces a comparison budget of 50,000–60,000 oracle calls per generated sample and evaluates Z-hat/Z plus Gaussian-mixture MMD and Wasserstein-2 distance. Settings include 60,000 AIS steps and 50 RDS time steps with T=5 and δ=0.005. V1 has no corresponding experimental protocol.

E4.justification: Figures 2–3 and Appendix I add qualitative mode-coverage diagnostics by overlaying generated samples on target-potential contours. These support analyses of inadequate mode exploration by TI/AIS. No component ablations or sensitivity sweeps are introduced.

E5.justification: V2 introduces empirical mean±standard-deviation reporting across 1,024 rounds, each averaging 1,024 independent trajectory estimates, and reports numerical-integration uncertainty for the Müller Brown reference constant. V1's variance bounds and median-trick discussion are theoretical rather than experimental uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: V2 adds all numerical results in Table 1 and sample findings in Figures 2–3. For the Gaussian mixture, Z-hat/Z is 0.2042±0.0008 for AIS, 1.0001±0.0850 for RDMC, and 0.9973±0.0834 for SNDMC. Results also reveal substantial variability, including Müller Brown RSDMC at 1.2885±12.7843. These evaluations have no v1 experimental counterpart.

T1.justification: V2 changes the AIS initialization complexity term from d^(3/2)/ε² to d^(4/3)/ε² while removing v1 Lemma 19 and its detailed Appendix H.2 proof. It changes Assumption 2 to exact stationarity at zero and extends the action lower bound to all r≥1. Appendix E corrects the RDS likelihood-ratio derivation, restores a missing dimension factor in the OU total-variation bound, and changes the SNDMC Hessian lower bound from βI to −βI. The principal action-dependent JE/AIS rates remain.

C1.justification: The central non-asymptotic JE/AIS complexity claims remain. V2's abstract and contributions additionally claim empirical effectiveness and superiority over AIS in handling multimodality, and describe the action lower bound as quantitatively explaining mass teleportation.

C2.justification: V2 adds comparisons between sampling and normalizing-constant estimation complexities, including an explanation of their different discretization requirements. It interprets the action lower bound through mass teleportation and the experiments through mode coverage. The conclusion newly identifies limited practical interpretability of action; the existing tightness uncertainty and drift-estimation tradeoff remain.

D1.justification: Appendix I adds target parameters, reference-integration instructions, algorithm hyperparameters, score-estimation sample counts, and metric software details. Algorithm 2 also explains how to generate its correlated Gaussian noises. Conversely, v1's detailed TI parameter derivation is removed. Reproduction of MMD remains problematic: Appendix I.3 lists a zero bandwidth and a normalized kernel inconsistent with the reported MMD magnitudes.

R1.justification: V2 substantially expands positioning through a new discussion of sampling beyond isoperimetry, computational hardness, and the relationship to Guo et al. (2025). It adds mass-teleportation literature and acknowledges an independently developed related proof in Chemseddine et al. (2025), alongside additional neural-sampling references. Publication updates to retained works are separate bibliographic edits.

P1.justification: V2 substantially reorganizes the narrative: much of v1's standalone preliminaries moves to Appendix A or the RDS section, while the problem-setting section gains motivating examples and a highlighted aim. Contributions, related work, the RDS discussion, and the conclusion are restructured. These changes extend beyond inserting experimental content.

P2.justification: V2 adds a six-method results table and two six-panel figures displaying samples against potential contours. The existing proof diagram remains Figure 1 but is resized and positioned before its explanatory sketch. A highlighted problem statement and substantial reflow further change the presentation.

improvement.justification: The corrected RDS work sign in Theorem 5, Algorithm 2, and Appendix E.3 removes a systematic multiplicative error in the proposed estimator, resolving an important correctness defect. Repeated-run experiments and implementation details provide useful additional validation. These gains outweigh reduced self-containment of the TI guarantee and weaknesses in the new empirical reporting, particularly the inconsistent MMD specification and broad accuracy claims despite large RSDMC variability.
